conventions: log score: higher is better; log-loss: its negative; d and 'minus': differences of log scores

qwen.technical_error_definition: a firm-card is an error when any draw used is invalid
qwen.raw_sums_draws: the draws used (fixed K = 1), valid answers also of firm-cards that are errors: they describe the answers, not the denominator

technical_error_flag.note: with differential errors only the against-the-claim sensitivity stands on equal footing with the main result; the symmetric worst case then favours the claim

coverage.note: the main result is the mean d among the firms with all used draws of both cards valid (complete cases at this K); a larger K or a model that fails more often removes more firms, so read it with the coverage and the error sensitivities

primary.estimand: mean d among firms with all used draws of both cards valid (complete cases)

without_sums_outside_range.note: answers with a raw sum outside (50, 200) treated as technical errors (plan F4)

primary.weighted_note: explanatory; SAFE weights are scaled within a wave, so in a development build (two waves) the weighted mean mixes two scales; in the test wave it does not

full_minus_shuffled.note: diagnostic, no test; an interval that includes 0 leaves open whether matching the other features to this firm improves the score

precision.note: since 0.7 the SD is the total SD of d over the size mix of the retained test sample (test size shares times this run's coverage by size class; class SDs and class means, as the unstratified bootstrap of the test sees them) and n the sum over classes of the test firms times the coverage of that class; test firms from --test-firms, size shares from the audit (no answers read)

k_rule.rule: K = 1 if the 80% upper bound < 0.2, 2 if < 0.5, else 3, with at least 20 firms (plan F1); the test averages the band log scores of the K draws of each card

d.note: from repeats of both cards on the same firms; var(d) of one draw is the mean of the two draws' variances; averaging K draws divides the noise part by K

stability.note: local model at temperature 0 with a fixed seed: near-deterministic, not exactly (the recorded repeats differ); a retry after an invalid answer usually repeats it

h3_full_vs_logit_segment.note: secondary, registered: the full card vs the statistical size x sector segmentation (logit on size and sector), in the graph with H1

level_check.rule: bounds_within_levels: every simultaneous one-sided upper bound of the claim-tail rate is at most its local level (diagnostic, any run). ready_for_freezing additionally needs a complete calibration: every model of the family, H1 and H3, both sample sizes and the three levels (36 bounds), at least 4000 outer replications and 10000 inner resamples, at most 1% replications without a p value, the K fixed per model with --k (the K of the test; a result for K = 1 does not approve K = 2 or 3), on development data. Every simultaneous one-sided upper bound of the claim-tail rate is at most its local level (0.0167, 0.025, 0.05); 0.0083 (alpha/3 split equally) is the reference, 0.0125 a diagnostic warning; not met = calibration not sufficiently confirmed, not proof of a faulty test; a changed procedure needs its own check before freezing; a met criterion covers the checked scenarios only

primary_family.comparisons: H1 full vs segment per model; H3 full vs logit_segment per model
primary_family.procedure: graphical (Bretz et al. 2009): alpha/3 on each H1, H1_i -> H3_i weight 1, H3_i -> H1_j (j != i) weight 1/2; p values directional (p if the mean difference > 0, else 1)
primary_family.scope: a rejection supports the claim for that model only
